catalog_quote: 2.1.2. Ударение динамическое. У именных разрядов слов и отглагольных имен падает на последний слог и при словообразовании постоянно переносится к исходу: kitkán ‘кукла’, kitkanə́k ‘куколка’, kitkandunə́k ‘место для кукол’. В глагольных основах (презентных, старых претеритальных и перфектных) ударение — на первом слоге: pы́rkṣ̌ыy ‘подслушивать’, прош. вр. pórkṣ̌oyd. Словоизменительные элементы, суффиксальные служебные элементы и разного рода энклитики не принимают на себя ударения: x̌ánəm ‘я скажу’, wúz-əm x̌átəy ‘я сказал(а)’, má-rək rándəv ‘дайте мне’, Не принимают ударения также показатели мн. числа имени: δə́γ̌d-išt ‘дочери’ (прям. п.), δə́γ̌d-əv (косв. п.). [Pakhalina & Lashkarbekov 1999: 175-176, read; Latin forms as printed, incl. the volume's Cyrillic ы inside Latin transcription and the cerebral ṣ̌ (caron + under-dot); the comma after ‘дайте мне’ is as printed] — Steblin-Kamensky 1999: 43, §75: Ударение (в ваханском силовое, но более слабое, чем в русском языке) в односложных словах падает, естественно, на единственный гласный, а в двусложных на гласный последнего слога [fn. 1] Засвидетельствовано также несколько слов с фиксированным ударением на первом слоге (например, bástək ‘ножницы’).

new_statements.quote: 2.1.2. Ударение динамическое. В глагольных основах (презентных, старых претеритальных и перфектных) ударение — на первом слоге: pы́rkšыy 'подслушивать', прош. вр. pórkšoyd. Словоизменительные элементы, суффиксальные служебные элементы и разного рода энклитики не принимают на себя ударения: x̌ánəm 'я скажу', wúz-əm x̌átəy 'я сказал(а)', má-rək rándəv 'дайте мне'. Не принимают ударения также показатели мн. числа имени: δə́γ̌d-išt 'дочери' (прям. п.), δə́γ̌d-əv (косв. п.).
new_statements.translation: 2.1.2. Stress is dynamic. In the nominal word classes and in deverbal nouns it falls on the last syllable and under word-formation is consistently shifted to the end: kitkán 'doll', kitkanák 'little doll', kitkandunák 'place for dolls'. In verb stems (present, old preterite and perfect) stress is on the first syllable: pы́rkšыy 'to eavesdrop', past pórkšoyd. Inflectional elements, suffixal function elements and enclitics of various kinds do not take stress: x̌ánəm 'I will say', wúz-əm x̌átəy 'I said', má-rək rándəv 'give (pl.) me'. The noun plural markers likewise do not take stress: δə́γ̌d-išt 'daughters' (direct case), δə́γ̌d-əv (oblique).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Dynamic (expiratory) stress on the final syllable of nouns, adjectives and other nominals, including derived stems (derivational suffixes attract stress to the new final syllable); inflectional suffixes (plural -išt/-əv, person endings) and enclitics stay unstressed, so stress is stem-final rather than strictly word-final; verb stems carry stress on their first syllable. Steblin-Kamensky 1999 §75 concurs: native words are mono/disyllabic with stress on the last syllable, verb forms have mobile stress governed by phrasal stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary stress in either source (Steblin-Kamensky notes only that compound verbs put main stress on the nominal part).
new_statements.exceptions: Verb stems: initial stress (P&L) / mobile stress depending on phrase stress, disyllabic imperatives mostly initial (Steblin-Kamensky §77); inflectional suffixes, plural markers and enclitics unstressed; Steblin-Kamensky p.43 fn.1: a few words with fixed initial stress, e.g. bástək 'scissors'; pretonic vowels reduce to ə (§76).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statements on citation forms; the stress domain for nominals is the derivational stem (inflection and clitics outside it). Steblin-Kamensky adds that ы~ə reduction in stressed final syllables happens only in connected speech under phrasal stress, and that verb-form stress interacts with phrasal stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Both deciding sources (Pakhalina & Lashkarbekov 2000; Steblin-Kamensky 1999) rest on Soviet-era fieldwork in the Tajikistan (right-bank Panj) Wakhan, upper and lower sub-dialects; they treat Wakhi as one language = wakh1245. Wakhi of Gojal/Hunza (Pakistan), Afghan Wakhan and Xinjiang is not separately described for stress in what I opened (Bashir 2009 would cover Pakistan Wakhi).

tone.quote: 本报告提供的数据和分析表明，在瓦罕塔吉克语里，词重音分布域是词汇词，成音节的派生词缀在重音分布域之内，而成音节的屈折词缀在重音分布域之外。双音节词汇词的第二音节是词重音的位置。[...] 第一，重音的主要物理相关物是音高，与时长以及音强的相关性不明显。 [提要:] 第一音节基频呈低平，第二音节基频呈高降或高平；当第二音节是开音节或以响辅音结尾时，基频呈高降；当第二音节以阻塞音结尾时，基频呈高平。
tone.locator: §五 结论 (Conclusion), points preamble + 第一; bracketed final sentence from the 提要 (abstract); e-edition, no page numbers
tone.translation: The data and analysis in this report show that in Wakhi Tajik the domain of word stress is the lexical word; syllabic derivational affixes are inside the stress domain while syllabic inflectional affixes are outside it. The second syllable of a disyllabic lexical word is the position of word stress. [...] First, the main physical correlate of stress is pitch; its correlation with duration and intensity is not evident. [Abstract:] The F0 of the first syllable is low level, that of the second syllable high-falling or high-level: high-falling when the second syllable is open or ends in a sonorant, high-level when it ends in an obstruent.

tone.quote: According to the results of both experiments, the most significant parameters for indicating a stressed syllable appear pitch frequency (F0) and duration (T), which mark stressed syllables in almost all the cases. Intensity (I) and its integral modification (I-area) also rise in the stressed syllable but this occurs less regularly. Statistically significant connection between stress and laryngeal parameters (subsonic frequency (Sub) and vertical larynx position) was not discovered at this stage of the study. Thus, the stress in the Wakhi language can be defined as quantitative-tonic.
